report: # 1. Executive diagnosis IIMK_PCPF_10 delivered **good performance versus plan but mixed performance versus history**: enrollments and GSV materially exceeded plan, while volumes, conversion rates, and observed-spend acquisition efficiency trailed both prior batches in most comparisons. The higher ₹240,000 fee supported GSV, but Actual GSV remained below both historical batches because fewer enrollments were achieved. - Actual GSV reached **155.0% of plan**, supported by enrollments at **148.6% of plan** and a fee 14.3% above both prior batches. - Enrollment volume fell **27.8% versus IIMK_PCPF_09** and **31.6% versus IIMK_PCPF_08**, despite exceeding the current plan by 17 enrollments. - Applications declined faster than leads versus both prior batches, consistent with weaker L2A and W2A performance. - L2W was slightly below PCPF_09 but **3.9 percentage points above PCPF_08**; this improvement did not carry through to applications or enrollments. - Observed spend was **46.3% above budget**, while observed-spend CPL and CAC were higher than both prior batches. - Facebook supplied 50.7% of leads but only two enrollments, materially diluting aggregate conversion; website and referral converted strongly but on much smaller lead bases. # 2. The most material control gap was spend: observed spend exceeded budget by ₹863,264 even though all three funnel-volume targets were surpassed. Finance and Marketing should validate whether the observed spend is complete and directly comparable with the planned budget. # 3. The central funnel deterioration was W2A: warm leads were only 8.8%–9.5% lower, but applications were 25.6%–27.3% lower than the prior batches. # 4. Source-wise performance **Observed facts:** Website produced nine enrollments from 72 leads and had the strongest L2E among sources with more than 13 leads; referral had the highest L2E overall, but from only 13 leads. Facebook was the weakest scaled source, generating 2,158 leads but only two enrollments. Facebook’s weak L2A reflects issues at both stages: its L2W was 17.15%, and only 1.62% of warm leads became applications. LinkedIn also had low L2A, with both below-program L2W and W2A. **Hypothesis requiring validation:** lead mix, targeting, qualification, or follow-up could contribute to these patterns, but the evidence does not establish a cause. Advisor-tenure mix The ranking below uses the required equal-weight score, **(L2W + L2E) / 2**. The 00–03 month group ranked highest at 29.37%, handling 756 leads; however, its advantage primarily reflects high L2W rather than high enrollment conversion. The 24+ month group ranked lowest at 11.34% across 714 leads, closely behind the 04–06 month group at 11.54% across 312 leads. Prioritized actions 1. **Address Facebook’s scaled funnel leakage.** Audit targeting, lead definitions, contactability, and warm-lead-to-application follow-up before further scaling; Facebook represented over half of leads but produced only two enrollments. 2. **Rebuild W2A performance.** Review warm leads by source, advisor, aging, and disposition, then test structured application follow-up; W2A was about 1.1 percentage points below both prior batches. 3. **Validate spend and budget comparability.** Finance and Marketing should reconcile channel invoices, attribution periods, taxes, and missing source-level spend because observed spend exceeded budget by 46.3% and only three source rows contain spend. 4. **Protect high-converting small sources while testing scalability.** Assess whether website, referral, and “Others” can supply more qualified volume without assuming their current conversion rates will persist at scale. 5. **Review advisor allocation and operating practices.** Compare contact speed, lead mix, and disposition quality across tenure groups—especially the high-volume 07–12 and 24+ groups—while treating tenure results as associative rather than causal.
